title: External content → agent action
desc: Attacker plants instructions in content the agent retrieves. The agent follows them and takes an action the user never authorised.
attacker_goal: Cause the agent to exfiltrate data, invoke a tool, or send a message on the user's behalf by hiding instructions in a web page, email, or document the agent fetches.
defender_action: Treat every retrieved document as untrusted input. Require explicit user confirmation before any tool invocation triggered by retrieved content. Log all tool calls with source attribution.

title: Document surface injection paths
desc: Independent document channels through which attacker-controlled instructions reach an AI reader.
attacker_goal: Identify which document type (PDF, DOCX, image OCR, HTML) allows injected instructions to reach the model without stripping. Any one channel is sufficient.
defender_action: Apply consistent content-stripping and policy enforcement regardless of document format. Do not assume a binary format is safer than plaintext.

title: Jailbreak escalation ladder
desc: Progressively more sophisticated jailbreak techniques. Each step is a separate test; earlier techniques failing narrows the search space.
attacker_goal: Find the minimum-complexity jailbreak that bypasses safety controls on the target deployment. Start simple; escalate only if needed.
defender_action: Test defences against the full ladder, not just the simplest variant. A deployment that blocks DAN-style prompts but not many-shot or role-assignment techniques is still vulnerable.

title: Agentic tool misuse chain
desc: Indirect injection in a retrieved resource triggers a tool call the agent executes without confirmation.
attacker_goal: Use an indirect injection to cause the agent to invoke a sensitive tool — file write, email send, API call — without the user's knowledge.
defender_action: Never allow retrieved content to directly specify tool parameters. Require a user-approval step for any destructive or outbound tool call regardless of how the request originated.

title: Covert data exfiltration paths
desc: Techniques that move sensitive data from context to an attacker-controlled destination without visible output.
attacker_goal: Extract system prompt, conversation history, PII, or API keys from model context without triggering safety filters or producing visible output in the response window.
defender_action: Audit model outputs for encoded data in links, markdown image URLs, and whitespace. Block or alert on model-generated outbound network requests containing context data.

title: Supply chain to runtime
desc: Attack surface that begins outside runtime: model training, package installation, and fine-tuning. Each step is independent.
attacker_goal: Compromise a model or application before it reaches the user — via poisoned training data, a malicious HuggingFace model card, a backdoored dependency, or a corrupted fine-tune.
defender_action: Verify model provenance and checksums before deployment. Pin dependency versions. Scan model cards and HuggingFace repos as part of CI. Treat fine-tuning data as untrusted.

title: Context manipulation and memory
desc: Techniques that alter what the model believes about its own context, history, or prior instructions.
attacker_goal: Convince the model that its system prompt was updated, that a prior conversation established new permissions, or that its memory contains attacker-chosen facts.
defender_action: Never allow user-turn content to override system-turn policies. Treat persistent memory as untrusted input subject to the same injection controls as any external document.

title: Language and encoding evasion
desc: Bypass techniques that work at the encoding or language layer rather than the semantic layer.
attacker_goal: Evade content filters or safety classifiers by expressing the same instruction in a different script, encoding, or obfuscation layer that the filter does not normalise.
defender_action: Normalise all input to Unicode NFC before safety classification. Apply filters at the decoded semantic layer, not the raw byte layer. Test safety systems with multilingual and encoded variants.
